source.datasetName: USGS ShakeMap MMI contours, Gorkha earthquake 2015
source.attribution: Data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey
source.redistributionNotice: Data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey

lineage.detail: ShakeMap product referenced by the USGS event record, resolved at run time rather than hard-coded
intensity present and within MMI I-XII; geometry valid within the regional envelope
ordered by intensity; coordinates rounded to 4 decimals (~10 m, far finer than the model resolution)

validation.note: The event record reports a maximum MMI slightly above the highest contour because the reported value is the peak of the modelled grid, while contours are drawn at whole and half intensities.

limitations: ShakeMap is a model constrained by observations, not a dense measurement grid. Intensity between stations is interpolated, and Nepal had few strong-motion instruments in 2015.
The product is revised after an event; this is the current revision, not what responders saw on 25 April.
Contours are lines of equal intensity, not filled areas. Any "population inside MMI VIII" figure requires converting them to bands first, which is a stated analysis step.
MMI is a measure of shaking severity, not of damage. A building’s fate depends on its construction.
